questions.q: According to the chapter, what distinguishes soul-tiredness from physical tiredness?
options: It is caused by a lack of sleep
It often remains even after the body has rested
It only affects people in full-time ministry
It always means there is unconfessed sin
questions.explanation: Physical tiredness may improve after sleep or a quiet weekend. Soul-tiredness often remains even after the body has rested, which is why trying harder rarely fixes it.

questions.q: When did Elijah sit down under the broom tree and ask God to let him die (1 Kings 19:4)?
options: After losing a public confrontation with the prophets of Baal
Before his ministry began, when he was still unknown
Immediately after his greatest public victory on Mount Carmel
After many years of quiet retirement
questions.explanation: Elijah did not break down after a defeat. He broke down after a triumph, once Jezebel's threat arrived and his body finally stopped (1 Kings 18–19).

questions.q: How did God first respond to Elijah under the broom tree (1 Kings 19:5–8)?
options: He rebuked Elijah for his lack of faith
He immediately gave Elijah new instructions
An angel gave him food and drink and let him sleep; direction came later
He sent Elijah straight back to confront Jezebel
questions.explanation: God met an exhausted prophet with rest first and direction second. Only after Elijah had eaten and slept, twice, did God lead him to Horeb and speak.

questions.q: In Mark 6:30–31, what did Jesus say to the disciples returning from their mission?
options: "Well done; now go out again"
"Come away by yourselves to a desolate place and rest a while"
"Why are you so tired? Have more faith"
"Stay with the crowds until everyone is fed"
questions.explanation: The disciples had no time even to eat. Jesus did not send them straight back out; he called them away to rest, the same rhythm he practised himself (Luke 5:16).

questions.q: What does the chapter say the goal of a spiritual reset is?
options: To produce a powerful emotional experience of God
To prove how spiritual you are
To force God to speak clearly about your future
To make yourself available to God, whatever you feel
questions.explanation: A spiritual reset is not an attempt to manufacture a feeling or force God to speak. It is a deliberate pause from noise and performance so you can become honest before God again.

questions.q: What does the chapter ask of readers who are thinking about harming themselves or may be in immediate danger?
options: Begin the retreat immediately, because silence will help
Do not begin the retreat alone; contact emergency or crisis services and tell a trusted person
Skip Part One and go straight to the sessions
Fast for three days before starting
questions.explanation: Silence can bring buried pain to the surface. Seeking help first is not a failure of faith; the chapter calls it an act of wisdom and courage.

reflection: When did you last feel close to God, not in a service or a meeting, but on your own? What was different then?
What is one thing you have kept doing for God while feeling nothing? Do not judge it. Just name it.
Elijah said, "It is enough." If you were completely honest with God right now, what would your sentence be?
